content: Etravirine is used in combination with at least two additional antiretroviral agents for the treatment of HIV-1 infection in treatment-experienced patients who exhibit viral replication and documented resistance to non-nucleoside reverse transcriptase inhibitors (NNRTIs). The standard dosage is 200 mg orally every 12 hours. No dosage adjustment is required for patients with mild-to-moderate hepatic impairment (Child-Pugh class A or B). However, pharmacokinetics have not been evaluated in patients with severe hepatic impairment (Child-Pugh class C). In pediatric patients aged 2 years or older with similar treatment experience and resistance profiles, etravirine may be used, but its safety and efficacy have not been established in children under 2 years of age. Etravirine interacts with various drugs by affecting hepatic and intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism, leading to either decreased or increased drug levels and effects. These interactions often result in contraindications or the need to avoid co-administration. Below are specific examples of such interactions: 1. Artemether/lumefantrine: Etravirine decreases their levels and effects by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Co-administration is contraindicated due to the risk of reduced antimalarial efficacy. 2. Carbamazepine: Etravirine levels are decreased by carbamazepine through CYP2C9/10 and CYP3A4 metabolism. Co-administration is contraindicated as it may lead to loss of virologic response and resistance to NNRTIs. 3. Cariprazine: Etravirine decreases cariprazine levels by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Co-administration is contraindicated because CYP3A4 is essential for cariprazine's active metabolite formation and elimination. 4. Cobicistat: Etravirine decreases cobicistat levels and effects via CYP3A4 metabolism. Co-administration is contraindicated as cobicistat increases etravirine levels, leading to potential adverse effects. 5. Fosamprenavir: Etravirine increases fosamprenavir levels by inhibiting its metabolism. Co-administration is contraindicated, whether or not low-dose ritonavir is used. 6. Indinavir: Etravirine decreases indinavir levels by inducing its metabolism. Co-administration is contraindicated. 7. Isavuconazonium sulfate: Etravirine decreases its levels and effects via CYP3A4 metabolism. Co-administration is contraindicated. 8. Lopinavir/ritonavir: Etravirine decreases lopinavir levels by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Co-administration is contraindicated. 9. Lumacaftor/ivacaftor: Etravirine decreases ivacaftor exposure by 57%, reducing its effectiveness. Co-administration is not recommended. 10. Mavacamten: Etravirine affects mavacamten levels through CYP2C19 and CYP3A4 metabolism. Co-administration is contraindicated due to the risk of altered drug exposure. 11. Naloxegol: Etravirine decreases naloxegol levels via CYP3A4 metabolism. Co-administration is contraindicated. 12. Nelfinavir: Etravirine increases nelfinavir levels by inhibiting its metabolism. Co-administration is contraindicated. 13. Nevirapine: Nevirapine decreases etravirine levels by inducing its metabolism. Co-administration is contraindicated, and combining etravirine with other NNRTIs is not recommended. 14. Ombitasvir/paritaprevir/ritonavir & dasabuvir (DSC): Etravirine decreases their levels and effects via CYP3A4 metabolism. Co-administration is contraindicated. 15. Pacritinib: Etravirine decreases pacritinib levels via CYP3A4 metabolism. Co-administration is contraindicated. 16. Panobinostat: Etravirine reduces panobinostat levels by approximately 70%, leading to treatment failure. Co-administration is contraindicated. 17. Phenobarbital: Phenobarbital decreases etravirine levels by inducing its metabolism. Co-administration is contraindicated. 18. Praziquantel: Etravirine decreases praziquantel levels via CYP3A4 metabolism. Discontinue etravirine two weeks before starting praziquantel and restart one day after the last praziquantel dose. 19. Regorafenib: Etravirine decreases regorafenib levels while increasing its active metabolite exposure. Co-administration is contraindicated. 20. Rifampin: Rifampin decreases etravirine levels by inducing its metabolism. Co-administration is contraindicated. 21. Rilpivirine: Etravirine decreases rilpivirine levels via CYP3A4 metabolism. Co-administration is contraindicated, and rilpivirine should not be used with NNRTIs. 22. Roflumilast: Etravirine decreases roflumilast levels and effects via CYP3A4 metabolism. Co-administration is not recommended. 23. St. John’s Wort: St. John’s Wort decreases etravirine levels via CYP3A4 metabolism. Co-administration is contraindicated. 24. Tipranavir/ritonavir: Tipranavir significantly decreases etravirine levels, leading to loss of therapeutic effect. Co-administration is contraindicated. 25. Vandetanib: Etravirine decreases vandetanib levels via CYP3A4 metabolism. Co-administration is contraindicated. 26. Velpatasvir: Etravirine decreases velpatasvir levels via CYP3A4 metabolism. Co-administration is contraindicated. 27. Abemaciclib: Etravirine decreases abemaciclib levels via CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 28. Afatinib: Etravirine increases afatinib levels via P-glycoprotein inhibition. Dose adjustment may be required. 29. Alpelisib: Etravirine decreases alpelisib levels via CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 30. Amiodarone: Etravirine decreases amiodarone levels via CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 31. Apalutamide: Apalutamide decreases etravirine levels via CYP2C19 and CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 32. Axitinib: Etravirine decreases axitinib levels via CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 33. Bedaquiline: Etravirine decreases bedaquiline levels via CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 34. Bosutinib: Etravirine decreases bosutinib levels via CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 35. Brigatinib: Etravirine decreases brigatinib levels via CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 36. Cabozantinib: Etravirine decreases cabozantinib levels via CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 37. Capivasertib: Etravirine decreases capivasertib levels via CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 38. Ceritinib: Etravirine decreases ceritinib levels via CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 39. Cimetidine: Cimetidine increases etravirine levels via CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 40. Clarithromycin: Clarithromycin increases etravirine levels via CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 41. Clopidogrel: Etravirine reduces clopidogrel efficacy by inhibiting CYP2C19 metabolism. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 42. Cobicistat: Etravirine decreases cobicistat levels via CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 43. Copanlisib: Etravirine decreases copanlisib levels via CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 44. Dabrafenib: Etravirine decreases dabrafenib levels via CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 45. Daridorexant: Etravirine decreases daridorexant levels via CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 46. Darunavir: Etravirine decreases darunavir levels via CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 47. Deflazacort: Etravirine decreases deflazacort levels via CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 48. Dihydroergotamine: Etravirine decreases dihydroergotamine levels via CYP3A4 metabolism. Co-administration is contraindicated. 49. Dihydroergotamine (intranasal): Etravirine decreases intranasal dihydroergotamine levels via CYP3A4 metabolism. Co-administration is contraindicated. This list highlights the importance of understanding drug interactions when prescribing etravirine, as many co-administered drugs require avoidance, substitution, or careful monitoring to prevent reduced efficacy or increased toxicity.
